title: Taxonomic status of the genera Amphipholis and Microphiopholis (Amphiuridae: Ophiuroidea): microstructural analyses
content:
Abstract
Microphiopholis Turner, 1985 has been characterized by the presence of a ventrodorsal perforation in the arm vertebra and disc covered by small scales. However, its validity has been questioned based on these characters. This study evaluates whether the perforation in the arm vertebra and the size of the scales are exclusive to Microphiopholis or related to a developmental stage. Altogether, 223 specimens from the Museum of Biological Diversity were analysed: 34 of Amphipholis januarii, 85 of A. squamata, 64 of Microphiopholis atra, and 40 of M. subtilis. Two developmental stages were established for each species. The external morphology was examined under a stereomicroscope, and the microstructures were studied using a scanning electron microscope. The vertebra perforation was observed in a juvenile of M. atra, an adult of A. squamata, and in both stages of M. subtilis, it was absent in A. januarii. We conclude that perforation of the arm vertebra and relative disc scale size are not diagnostic characters of Microphiopholis and are not related to growth, as no consistent pattern was observed at any particular developmental stage. We propose synonymizing the two genera under Amphipholis. The dental and oral plates of M. atra and M. subtilis are described for the first time.
